In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

descriptor_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: rotational entropy loss under confinement. draft.name: rotational_clearance_ratio_Dif_GeDi
draft.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss is partly governed by rotational confinement (E01, E02, E04), then at fixed framework identity the dimensionless ratio GeDi/(GeDi+lsd_p) increases the predicted entropy loss over R: adsorbates whose largest atom-pair distance GeDi approaches the largest included-sphere diameter along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) have less local rotational space and are hypothesized to lose a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy upon adsorption.
draft.rationale: Mechanism: rotational entropy loss under confinement. The included-along-free-path diameter Dif (lsd_p) is used as a proxy for the local included rotational space along the diffusion path; it is explicitly NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT the global cavity diameter Di, so frameworks with large cages connected by narrow windows may be mischaracterized. GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair-distance proxy for the adsorbate's longest span and ignores hydrogen extent; its legitimate zeros (54 single-site cases) are preserved, mapping those rows to descriptor value 0 rather than imputing a median. The bounded sum form keeps the descriptor finite on the full training support and dimensionless, so no fitted constants are introduced. AV is deliberately not used here because it is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, and would invite an invalid AV/Vol free-volume claim.
draft.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is falsified if: (1) the empirical sign of entropy loss versus GeDi at fixed lsd_p is negative (less loss for larger adsorbates), contradicting the rotational-confinement hypothesis; (2) translational-loss proxies (e.g., ASA/AV) alone explain the target and the GeDi/lsd_p ratio adds no conditional information; (3) frameworks where Dif strongly underestimates cavity size (large cages behind narrow windows) show low entropy loss despite high descriptor values, indicating Dif is the wrong confinement proxy and global Di would be required.

variable_mappings.lsd_p: included_along_free_path_Dif (Zeo++ Dif, largest included sphere along free-sphere path; NOT bottleneck Df, NOT global cavity Di)

draft.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (not established): (a) Dif is an acceptable proxy for local included rotational space along the adsorption path, even though it is neither the passing bottleneck Df nor the global cavity Di; (b) GeDi (heavy-atom, implicit-H) is an acceptable proxy for the adsorbate rotational span; (c) rotational entropy loss varies monotonically with the GeDi/Dif clearance, consistent with the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU comparisons, whose percentages and conditions are not transferred as constants; (d) infinite-dilution, rigid-framework transfer from the source zeolite studies remains a hypothesis.
draft.boundary_behavior: Finite on full training support: q_lsd_p has minimum 3.3452/lsd_p_ref > 0, so the denominator never vanishes; q_GeDi = 0 for the 54 legitimate single-site zeros yields descriptor value 0 (no pair-distance confinement signal), preserving native zeros without imputation. Descriptor range on training support is [0, 1) and approaches but never reaches 1 because q_lsd_p > 0.

review_issues.explanation: Hypothesis-vs-formula mismatch: the narrative states 'GeDi/(GeDi+lsd_p)' and 'GeDi approaches the largest included-sphere diameter lsd_p', but the formula uses q-normalized values with DIFFERENT references (GeDi_ref=3.302656784 angstrom, lsd_p_ref=6.38663 angstrom). Per the normalization constraint, q-ratio=1 is not native equality; the descriptor's implicit native equality point is GeDi = (GeDi_ref/lsd_p_ref) x lsd_p = ~0.517 x lsd_p, not GeDi = lsd_p. The clearance-ratio story is therefore shifted by a constant factor relative to what the formula computes.

Representation mismatch in the ratio: GeDi is an implicit-H/heavy-atom pair distance (hydrogen extent ignored), while lsd_p derives from full framework geometric sphere calculations. Comparing a heavy-atom span to a full-geometry included sphere systematically understates the adsorbate extent; this matters because the training domain is alkali/alkane-dominated where hydrogens contribute substantially to rotational span.

Proxy substitution asserted as established: E02 names the average cavity diameter (Di) as the confinement descriptor; lsd_p is Zeo++ Dif (largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path), which is explicitly NOT Di and not necessarily the sphere at the adsorption site. Entropy loss occurs at the adsorption site, not along the diffusion path; the mapping 'Dif = local rotational space at the adsorption site' is a hypothesis. The draft acknowledges the large-cage-behind-narrow-window failure mode only in falsification criteria while the hypothesis text asserts the mapping unconditionally.

Direction-of-effect extrapolation: the quoted comparisons (E01: MFI vs FAU rotational DOF loss; E04: 38% vs 20% entropy loss for linear alkanes) vary the FRAMEWORK at roughly fixed adsorbate. The within-framework direction claimed in the hypothesis (at fixed lsd_p, larger GeDi implies larger entropy loss) is not stated in any quoted source; monotonicity of loss over the full training range is extrapolated from two-point framework comparisons. Source percentages (3-fold, 38%, 20%, 4.3 A / 13 A) must not become constants or thresholds.

E06 motivates a radius-of-gyration vs available-space comparison, qualitatively and specific to MCM-22 supercages (linear/singly-branched molecules, diffusion discussed at 450-850 K). GeDi (maximum atom-pair distance) is a different shape measure from radius of gyration, and the cage-specific reasoning is not transferred; the source itself only 'proposes a possible effect' on adsorption equilibrium.

Single-site zero handling: for the 54 legitimate GeDi=0 rows the descriptor is identically 0. For single-atom adsorbates rotational degrees of freedom do not exist, so the rotational-loss mechanism is degenerate there; labeling descriptor 0 as 'preserving native zeros' conflates 'no rotation possible' with 'no rotational confinement signal' and places these rows at the least-confinement end of the [0,1) range. This interpretation is a modeling choice, not an established physical mapping.

Flat region: at q_GeDi=0 the descriptor and its gradient vanish with respect to lsd_p (and every framework input), so the descriptor cannot rank frameworks for the 54 single-site adsorbates. Elsewhere the descriptor is smooth and monotone decreasing in lsd_p (d/d lsd_p = -q_GeDi/(lsd_p_ref x (q_GeDi+q_lsd_p)^2) < 0), consistent with expression_check.descriptor_direction='decreasing', but the flat zero region limits conditional use across the full training support.

The physical prediction (vary lsd_p, hold GeDi, loss decreasing) is internally consistent with the formula and with the framework-side variation the sources actually report, but the hypothesis additionally asserts an adsorbate-side monotone claim (increasing GeDi at fixed lsd_p increases loss) that is stated as the mechanism while being supported only by analogy, not by any quoted within-framework comparison.

Execution-check discrepancy: the recorded rejection reason ('Wrong physical variable mapping: GeDi requires heavy_atom_pair_distance') appears inconsistent with the draft's declared variable_mappings, which does map GeDi to heavy_atom_pair_distance. This review records the discrepancy without resolving or overriding it; scientific_consistency remains 'unverified'.

These absences do not falsify the proxy or mechanism; they only mean the knowledge graph does not document support for them. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

draft.name: rotational_clearance_ratio_Dif_GeDi
draft.hypothesis: If adsorption entropy loss is partly governed by rotational confinement (E01, E02, E04), then at fixed framework identity the dimensionless ratio GeDi/(GeDi+lsd_p) increases the predicted entropy loss over R: adsorbates whose largest atom-pair distance GeDi approaches the largest included-sphere diameter along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) have less local rotational space and are hypothesized to lose a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy upon adsorption.
draft.rationale: Mechanism: rotational entropy loss under confinement. The included-along-free-path diameter Dif (lsd_p) is used as a proxy for the local included rotational space along the diffusion path; it is explicitly NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT the global cavity diameter Di, so frameworks with large cages connected by narrow windows may be mischaracterized. GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair-distance proxy for the adsorbate's longest span and ignores hydrogen extent; its legitimate zeros (54 single-site cases) are preserved, mapping those rows to descriptor value 0 rather than imputing a median. The bounded sum form keeps the descriptor finite on the full training support and dimensionless, so no fitted constants are introduced. AV is deliberately not used here because it is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, and would invite an invalid AV/Vol free-volume claim.
draft.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is falsified if: (1) the empirical sign of entropy loss versus GeDi at fixed lsd_p is negative (less loss for larger adsorbates), contradicting the rotational-confinement hypothesis; (2) translational-loss proxies (e.g., ASA/AV) alone explain the target and the GeDi/lsd_p ratio adds no conditional information; (3) frameworks where Dif strongly underestimates cavity size (large cages behind narrow windows) show low entropy loss despite high descriptor values, indicating Dif is the wrong confinement proxy and global Di would be required.

review_issues.explanation: Hypothesis-vs-formula mismatch: the narrative states 'GeDi/(GeDi+lsd_p)' and 'GeDi approaches the largest included-sphere diameter lsd_p', but the formula uses q-normalized values with DIFFERENT references (GeDi_ref=3.302656784 angstrom, lsd_p_ref=6.38663 angstrom). Per the normalization constraint, q-ratio=1 is not native equality; the descriptor's implicit native equality point is GeDi = (GeDi_ref/lsd_p_ref) x lsd_p = ~0.517 x lsd_p, not GeDi = lsd_p. The clearance-ratio story is therefore shifted by a constant factor relative to what the formula computes.

Representation mismatch in the ratio: GeDi is an implicit-H/heavy-atom pair distance (hydrogen extent ignored), while lsd_p derives from full framework geometric sphere calculations. Comparing a heavy-atom span to a full-geometry included sphere systematically understates the adsorbate extent; this matters because the training domain is alkali/alkane-dominated where hydrogens contribute substantially to rotational span.

Proxy substitution asserted as established: E02 names the average cavity diameter (Di) as the confinement descriptor; lsd_p is Zeo++ Dif (largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path), which is explicitly NOT Di and not necessarily the sphere at the adsorption site. Entropy loss occurs at the adsorption site, not along the diffusion path; the mapping 'Dif = local rotational space at the adsorption site' is a hypothesis. The draft acknowledges the large-cage-behind-narrow-window failure mode only in falsification criteria while the hypothesis text asserts the mapping unconditionally.

Direction-of-effect extrapolation: the quoted comparisons (E01: MFI vs FAU rotational DOF loss; E04: 38% vs 20% entropy loss for linear alkanes) vary the FRAMEWORK at roughly fixed adsorbate. The within-framework direction claimed in the hypothesis (at fixed lsd_p, larger GeDi implies larger entropy loss) is not stated in any quoted source; monotonicity of loss over the full training range is extrapolated from two-point framework comparisons. Source percentages (3-fold, 38%, 20%, 4.3 A / 13 A) must not become constants or thresholds.

E06 motivates a radius-of-gyration vs available-space comparison, qualitatively and specific to MCM-22 supercages (linear/singly-branched molecules, diffusion discussed at 450-850 K). GeDi (maximum atom-pair distance) is a different shape measure from radius of gyration, and the cage-specific reasoning is not transferred; the source itself only 'proposes a possible effect' on adsorption equilibrium.

Single-site zero handling: for the 54 legitimate GeDi=0 rows the descriptor is identically 0. For single-atom adsorbates rotational degrees of freedom do not exist, so the rotational-loss mechanism is degenerate there; labeling descriptor 0 as 'preserving native zeros' conflates 'no rotation possible' with 'no rotational confinement signal' and places these rows at the least-confinement end of the [0,1) range. This interpretation is a modeling choice, not an established physical mapping.

Flat region: at q_GeDi=0 the descriptor and its gradient vanish with respect to lsd_p (and every framework input), so the descriptor cannot rank frameworks for the 54 single-site adsorbates. Elsewhere the descriptor is smooth and monotone decreasing in lsd_p (d/d lsd_p = -q_GeDi/(lsd_p_ref x (q_GeDi+q_lsd_p)^2) < 0), consistent with expression_check.descriptor_direction='decreasing', but the flat zero region limits conditional use across the full training support.

The physical prediction (vary lsd_p, hold GeDi, loss decreasing) is internally consistent with the formula and with the framework-side variation the sources actually report, but the hypothesis additionally asserts an adsorbate-side monotone claim (increasing GeDi at fixed lsd_p increases loss) that is stated as the mechanism while being supported only by analogy, not by any quoted within-framework comparison.

Execution-check discrepancy: the recorded rejection reason ('Wrong physical variable mapping: GeDi requires heavy_atom_pair_distance') appears inconsistent with the draft's declared variable_mappings, which does map GeDi to heavy_atom_pair_distance. This review records the discrepancy without resolving or overriding it; scientific_consistency remains 'unverified'.

Absent graph support is unknown, not disproof: no mechanism card lists GeDi under C1/C4 (framework-entropy-loss mechanisms), and no edge ties the descriptor to a within-framework adsorbate-size direction. These absences do not falsify the proxy or mechanism; they only mean the knowledge graph does not document support for them.
